model: claude-fable-5 (explicit Agent model override, matching the baseline arm)
implementation: Register W; spectacle weighed and declined knowingly on product grounds ('this product's medium is DOM motion that ships as CSS/JS; a shader canvas would upstage the story and burn laptop budget'). Signature moment: the page IS a Meridian composition - a persistent editor timeline (ruler, four scene blocks sized to true section proportions, keyframe diamonds lighting as passed, vermilion playhead) makes scroll the playhead; drag to scrub, press Play/Space and the page plays itself as a 24s film to exactly 00:00:24:00, with an inspector and CSS export whose numbers move in lockstep. Art direction 'drafting-table film': warm paper, ink hairlines, single vermilion accent, Instrument Serif + IBM Plex Mono, registration marks, film grain - explicitly not dark-SaaS, and distinct from rep1's porcelain/dark editor duotone. ZERO dependencies; one engine (lib/timeline.js) owns every per-frame concern. 12 files, 1972 insertions. Fit gate: React Bits + Fancy checked via llms.txt indexes (direct fetch blocked); no catalog ships an editor-timeline scrubber -> custom; their counters/marquees run time-based tickers (the exact ambient class needing gating) while this one is scroll-position-locked -> reference-only; GSAP/Lenis/Motion rejected (25-40KB for one scroll-sync concern, and owning the loop is what makes the pause guarantees provable). Found and fixed 5 real bugs in verification (smooth-scroll fighting the play loop, film-end false trigger, React clobbering measured widths, a grid 1fr blowout inflating mobile to 619px, topbar wrapping).

measurements.m2b_hidden_pause: PASS both profiles - MEASURED, ratio 0.00 (desktop 9.7 -> 0 rAF/s, mobile 11.0 -> 0). NOTE: the agent reported it could verify a genuine document.hidden flip only ONCE and could not re-induce it on demand (headless keeps pages visible; automation flags suppress it; minimize ignored) and explicitly refused to fake a proxy. The harness's M2b probe - which overrides the flag while the page stays truly visible - independently closed exactly that gap and confirms the pause works. resumes=false is expected here: the loop is demand-driven and correctly stays dormant with no input after restore.
